When we want to add emphasis to a verb, we often stress the auxiliary. We do this especially when we want to correct what somebody said or contrast it with something else.

The emphatic do is more common in spoken than in written English. You can use the emphasis with do when you are speaking in simple present, you can also express emphasis using does when you emphasize about someone else.

We use it to:
- stress a strong affirmation about something.
- confirm something we think it is true, following it with a question tag.

Examples:
  • I do arrive on time, I even took a taxi.
  • We do want to help you.
  • Do you work every day? I do work every day, even Sundays!

Simple past, Types of Irregular Verbs
Irregular verbs are verbs that don't take on the regular –d, -ed, or -ied spelling patterns of the simple past.

We use the Simple Past to express the idea that an action started and finished at a specific time in the past. We use the Simple Past to list a series of completed actions in the past.

images.text:
Amy: Do you know anything about DOM? I am preparing the slides for tomorrow's presentation. Yesterday, I read a long document and the presentation isn't ready yet.
Kevin: I do know about DOM. It's actually the best part of my job.
Amy: Yeah, I thought you could help me. Do you have time?
Kevin: I do have time if it is for DOM!
Amy: Thanks. Let's start with the concept.

Kevin: I chose a good book that you're going to find attractive and helpful. It says DOM stands for Document Object Model. It's a way to represent a Web document like HTML, as an object that a software developer can manipulate using the code in a scripting language like JavaScript, and it was created by the World Wide Web Consortium to standardize web pages access.
Amy: So, we can say that DOM expresses the rational structure of any document and the best way for developers getting into and managing that document.
Kevin: Exactly. It does define the logical structure; also, using DOM a programmer can build documents, navigate through the hierarchical structure of a document, add, modify, or delete content.

Amy: It sounds really useful, but does it have any drawbacks?
Kevin: It does have a big drawback. Learning the DOM methods and learning how to use them takes some time for new programmers.
Amy: What about the advantages? Does it have any?
Kevin. It does have some benefits. DOM makes it easier to write tools to process them in a series of steps and processing can be faster than using other models. Finally, DOM is easy to understand because it lets programmers have a complete access to the document as a whole and the capacity to operate through the entire composition.
Amy: Thanks, Kevin. Now my slides have reliable information; your help was remarkable.
